solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Ornament fashion designer turned into coal

indicators.note: something turned round faces the other way, so the designer's name is read from its end
going into something means being placed inside it, so the designer sits within the coal

blocks.note: an ember is a glowing piece of coal
Christian Dior, the French couturier

explanation.surface: A couturier's dress design is somehow worked into a lump of coal.
explanation.walkthrough: DIOR turned is ROID, which goes into EMB-ER to give EMBROIDER.
explanation.definitionFit: To embroider is to decorate cloth with needlework, i.e. to ornament it as a verb.

clue.text: Almost simple to grab first of the food

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the word is dropped
the first of a word is just its opening letter
grabbing something means holding it, so one piece is wrapped round another

blocks.note: simple means easy; almost all of it is kept
opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Snatching the first bite of a meal ought to be nearly effortless.
explanation.walkthrough: EASY loses its Y to leave EAS, which grabs T: EA(T)S.
explanation.definitionFit: Eats is informal slang for food, as in 'let's get some eats'.

blocks.note: surface reading: the one credential that matters most for a job
setter's reading: single means unmarried, so the fitting award for a single person is one named after an unmarried man

explanation.walkthrough: 'Single' looks like 'only one', but it means unmarried, and an unmarried man is a bachelor.
explanation.definitionFit: A first university award such as a BA or BSc is named after the bachelor, a word that also describes an unmarried man.

clue.text: Stone walls crushed into something extra?

definitions.note: a noun phrase for an adjective; the question mark admits the stretch, as in 'an optional extra'

indicators.note: crushed things are pounded out of shape, so the letters are rearranged
a wall encloses what is inside it, so the stone surrounds the other letters

blocks.note: opal is a gemstone
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A stone wall gets smashed into rubble that nobody actually needed.
explanation.walkthrough: OPAL walls a rearranged INTO: OP(TION)AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something optional is not required, a possible addition one may take or leave, like an optional extra on a car.

indicators.note: something shot is ruined or broken, so the letters before it are rearranged

blocks.note: D is the standard abbreviation for daughter
the four letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A daughter has a jab and then takes a turn at doing it herself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' appears twice: first as an injection in the definition, then as 'wrecked' for the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: To be dosed is to have been given a measured amount of medicine, such as a shot or injection.

clue.text: Pants are hiding nothing that's nasty, I'd guess

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish or badly done, so the word next to it is jumbled
hiding something means concealing it inside, so the jumbled word surrounds the rest

blocks.note: the three letters rearranged and split to enclose
zero, shaped like the letter O
ugh is the exclamation of disgust
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Someone surmises, with disgust, that a pair of trousers are concealing nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' looks like the subject, trousers, but it is the British slang anagram signal. REA holds O, UGH and I'D: R(OUGHID)EA.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough idea is an approximate notion, an estimate, which is what a guess is.

indicators.note: after places one piece behind the other, here confirming the order of the two parts

blocks.note: per annum, Latin for 'a year', abbreviated p.a.
informal yes, i.e. certainly

explanation.surface: Twelve months on, a debtor is told to clear what is owed without fail.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle a bill or debt is to hand over the money owed.

blocks.note: surface reading: a fragment of something remembered from growing up
setter's reading: piece is slang for a gun, so this is a toy weapon one recalls from being small

explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece' suggests a fragment of a memory; in gangster slang a piece is a firearm.
explanation.definitionFit: A toy weapon that fires a cork with a bang is a classic plaything children remember from their early years.

blocks.note: surface reading: the proverb that it is better to give than to receive
setter's reading: the phrase tells a gift-giver they ought not to have it themselves but give it, and it is also the polite thanks on receiving a present

explanation.walkthrough: Read literally the phrase says owning is wrong and giving is better, echoing the proverb, while in use it is what a grateful recipient says.
explanation.definitionFit: The polite exclamation on receiving a present expresses gratitude while modestly protesting the giver's generosity.

clue.text: Media mogul to continue drinking in pub

indicators.note: drinking in means taking something inside, so one piece swallows the other

blocks.note: to press on is to keep going
a bar is a pub

explanation.surface: A newspaper tycoon carries on boozing in the local.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drinking in' fits the pub scene so well that it reads as plain surface, but it is the signal to put one piece inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: A press baron is a powerful newspaper owner, a mogul of the print media.

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it within, so the word for diplomacy encloses another piece

blocks.note: tact is diplomacy in dealing with people
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Being diplomatic often means keeping your mouth shut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diplomacy' looks like the definition, but the answer is an adjective, so the definition must be 'silent'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacit means understood without being spoken aloud, so unspoken or silent, as in tacit agreement.

blocks.note: first meaning: the craft of carving or modelling three-dimensional works
second meaning: a shaped piece, or to shape by carving

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one phrase, 'an art form', but splits into two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Sculpture is both the fine art of carving and modelling and a carved piece or the act of shaping, i.e. a form.

blocks.note: surface reading: worrying over tiny particulars, an obsessive's fretting
setter's reading: a minute is made up of sixty small parts, so musings about those units are reconsiderations

explanation.walkthrough: 'Minute' looks like 'tiny', but it is the unit of time, whose details are its sixty seconds.
explanation.definitionFit: Second thoughts are doubts or misgivings about a decision, a form of anxiety; cryptically, thoughts about the parts of a minute.

clue.text: Drive cook to see PR expert

blocks.note: a drive or a spin is a short trip in a car
to cook or doctor figures is to falsify them

explanation.surface: A chef is driven off to meet a public-relations consultant.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'Drive' and 'cook' look like verbs of action, but they stand for a car outing and fiddling the books.
explanation.definitionFit: A spin doctor is a publicist who presents news in the most favourable light, a public-relations specialist.

clue.text: Information from lawyer sought by atheist?

indicators.note: what is sought by someone is wanted after them, so this piece follows the other in the answer

blocks.note: pro-pagan: someone in favour of the heathen rather than the faithful, a whimsical stretch the question mark flags
DA is a District Attorney, an American prosecutor

explanation.surface: An unbeliever is looking for a lawyer to get some facts.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark excuses treating an atheist as pro-pagan; DA is the American District Attorney.
explanation.definitionFit: Propaganda is information, often biased or misleading, spread to promote a cause.

blocks.note: first meaning: a quality or characteristic belonging to something
second meaning: to ascribe or credit something to a cause or person

explanation.walkthrough: 'Property charge' reads like a fee on real estate; the two words are separate meanings, a noun and a verb stressed differently.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it is a characteristic quality; as a verb it means to assign blame or credit, as in to charge a fault to someone.

clue.text: Head back to get a fish

indicators.note: going back means travelling the other way, so the word for head is read from its end

blocks.note: nut is slang for the head
taken as written

explanation.surface: An angler returns to the river hoping to land a catch.
explanation.walkthrough: Nut is everyday slang for the head, as in 'use your nut'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuna is a large ocean fish, a species of the mackerel family.

indicators.note: wrestling twists and contorts a body, so the letters are twisted into a new order

blocks.note: the five letters rearranged
ned is Scottish slang for a young hooligan or yob

explanation.surface: Someone exploited their strength to grapple with a thug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Used' looks like the verb of the surface, but it is the adjective definition. A ned is a Scottish yob.
explanation.definitionFit: Pre-owned is a euphemism for secondhand, as goods that have already been used by someone else.

indicators.note: in means the letters lie inside the words that follow, running across the gap between them

blocks.note: the letters sit across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Someone notices the chill most in their fingers.
explanation.walkthrough: NESH is an English dialect word, chiefly northern and Midlands, for someone who feels the cold easily.
explanation.definitionFit: Nesh is dialect for unusually sensitive to cold weather, so it describes a person who is always feeling chilly.

clue.text: Made to air broadcast on small wireless

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, as seed is sown, so the letters are spread into a new order
on places one piece beside another, here the anagram coming after the single letter

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
the nine letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Something was produced for transmission on a little radio set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' and 'air' suggest radio and so does the answer, which makes the anagram signal easy to miss. Steam radio is a jocular British term for old-fashioned radio.
explanation.definitionFit: Wireless is the old-fashioned British word for a radio set, and steam radio is a humorous term for the same old medium.

clue.text: Bottle that may be full of slugs

definitions.text: that may be full of slugs

blocks.note: first meaning: a large wine bottle holding twice the standard amount

blocks.clueFragment: that may be full of slugs
blocks.note: second meaning: a powerful handgun, loaded with bullets, slugs being slang for bullets

explanation.walkthrough: 'Slugs' suggests garden pests or slugs of drink, but it is slang for bullets.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnum is both an oversized wine bottle and a high-powered revolver whose cartridges hold bullets.

blocks.note: surface reading: what a playhouse spends on staff, heating and productions
setter's reading: the theatre is a hospital surgical room, so its spending is what surgery costs

explanation.walkthrough: 'Theatre' suggests a stage, but in a hospital it is the room where surgeons work.
explanation.definitionFit: Running expenses of a business are its day-to-day outgoings; cryptically, the bills of a surgical suite.

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
a rasp is a coarse file

explanation.surface: Keep hold of a decent nail file.
explanation.definitionFit: To grasp something is to grip it firmly, so to hold it.

blocks.note: cha or char is British slang for tea
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Teatime is when the neighbours swap rumours.
explanation.definitionFit: A chat is an informal conversation, the kind of talk that gossip is.

clue.text: Being hairy thanks to a natural mutation

indicators.note: a mutation is a change in form, so the letters of the word before it are altered in order

blocks.note: ta is British informal for thanks
the seven letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone has grown furry, owing to a genetic quirk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being' looks like 'existing as', but it is a noun: a creature. 'Thanks to a natural mutation' reads as TA plus a mutation of NATURAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarantula is a large spider covered in bristly hair, so it is a hairy creature.

blocks.note: smart means neat in appearance
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A chic place to stay in a town in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: Neath is a town in south Wales, near Swansea.
explanation.definitionFit: Neath is an industrial town in south Wales, so it is a Welsh town by example.

clue.text: Watery stuff he found in drink

indicators.note: something found in another is sitting inside it, so one piece is placed within the other

blocks.note: rum is an alcoholic drink
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man discovers something watery at the bottom of his glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watery stuff' sounds like a weak drink, but it is the old word for mucus or tears.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheum is a thin watery discharge from the eyes or nose, as with a cold.

blocks.note: first meaning: suitable or advantageous for the purpose
second meaning: a device or method used to achieve an end

explanation.walkthrough: 'Means' looks like the verb 'signifies', as if a dictionary entry; it is the noun, a way of doing something.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means convenient and suitable; as a noun an expedient is a stopgap method or resource.
